You've got tokens: a sequence of numbers. Next question is, what does the model *do* with them?

---

After tokenization, each token number gets looked up in a giant table of **embeddings** — lists of hundreds of numbers that place the token in a mathematical space where *meaning* starts to emerge.

Tokens with similar meanings end up close together in this space. "King" and "queen" are near each other. "Bank" (river) and "bank" (money) start at the same point — but the surrounding tokens will pull them in different directions.

Then the model runs those embeddings through layers of **attention**, where every token looks at every other token and asks: *which of you matters most for figuring out what I mean?*

[EX]In "I went to the bank to fish," the word "fish" pulls "bank" toward the river meaning. In "I went to the bank to deposit a check," "deposit" pulls it the other way. Attention is what makes that disambiguation happen.[/EX]

[KEY]Embeddings turn token numbers into meaningful coordinates, and attention lets every token influence the interpretation of every other token.[/KEY]

[Q]
Why does the word "bank" get interpreted differently depending on the sentence?
A) The tokenizer assigns it a different number each time
B) The attention mechanism lets surrounding tokens shift its meaning
C) The model looks up the correct definition in a dictionary
ANS: B
[/Q]

Nicely done. Now for the second micro-concept.

Once your prompt is a list of token-numbers, the model needs to figure out which tokens *matter most* to each other. That's where the **attention mechanism** comes in.

Attention lets the model weigh relationships between tokens — no matter how far apart they are in the sentence.

[EX]In the sentence "The trophy didn't fit in the suitcase because it was too big" — what does "it" refer to? The trophy. Attention is the mechanism that lets the model connect "it" back to "trophy" across several tokens, rather than just looking at the word right before it.[/EX]

This is what makes transformers so powerful compared to older models that read text strictly left-to-right with no long-range memory.

[KEY]Attention lets the model dynamically connect any token to any other token in the prompt, capturing meaning across distance.[/KEY]

[Q]
Why does the attention mechanism matter?
A) It lets the model look up facts in a database
B) It helps the model connect related words even when they're far apart in a sentence
C) It stores the conversation in the model's long-term memory
ANS: B
[/Q]
